routes.label: Relate the click rate to speed

question: The rails on a railroad are \(30\) feet long. As the train passes over the point where the rails are joined, there is an audible click. The speed of the train in miles per hour is approximately the number of clicks heard in:
solution:
Use the intended model of one effective click for each \(30\)-foot rail passed, with the train moving at a steady positive speed. Let its speed be \(v\) miles per hour. Since a mile is \(5280\) feet and an hour is \(3600\) seconds, the click rate is
\[
\frac{5280v}{30\cdot3600}
=\frac{11v}{225}
\quad\text{clicks per second}.
\]
The click count over \(t>0\) seconds is therefore approximately \(11vt/225\). For that count to equal the numerical speed \(v\), we want
\[
\frac{11vt}{225}=v.
\]
Because \(v>0\), we may divide by \(v\), giving
\[
t=\frac{225}{11}\approx20.45\text{ seconds}.
\]
Counting whole clicks can introduce an endpoint difference of one click. The appropriate approximate interval among the choices is \(20\) seconds, choice A.
